_schema: One JSON object per line. Fields: timestamp (ISO 8601), section (NN), paragraph (int, 1-based), claim_text (string, max 200 chars), support_type (evidence-card | footnote | unmapped), support_ref (path to evidence card OR footnote number OR null), reason (string, only present when support_type=unmapped, one of: evidence-gap | not-yet-harvested | requires-primary-source | intentional-conjecture), audited_in_run (int, the run_count when this claim was first audited), confidence (float 0-1, agent's confidence in the mapping). Initial seed entry below; the verify-provenance sub-task appends one entry per claim per section per audit run.

claim_text: The vault is published at https://constitutionallaw.netlify.app.
The corpus snapshot is 198 pages: 92 case briefs, 27 doctrinal topic pages, and 79 lecture summaries.
The 198-page snapshot was captured as of a fixed progress-report date (the same report anchoring Section IV); the explicit as-of date is not stated in prose or footnote.
The deployed site, not the local vault on disk, is the artifact a student or peer reviewer opens; the vault on disk is the upstream source the build script reads.
The build is one Python script, .site/build.py, supported by three hand-written shell files: index.html, app.js, and style.css.
The build.py script is approximately 700 lines.

The script walks Cases/Topics/Lectures, parses YAML frontmatter, renders markdown with markdown-it, resolves Obsidian wiki-links into hash routes of the form #/p/<kind>/<slug>, and extracts a holding-bar and citation-metadata block per case page.

The build writes three JSON artifacts into .site/dist/: pages.json (full corpus with rendered HTML and search text), manifest.json (lightweight index for navigation and counts), and search.json (compact text index for the search palette).

The runtime shell loads the JSON artifacts client-side, defines hash-route navigation reaching every page, wires a Cmd-K search palette to search.json, and registers a Netlify page-feedback form stub at build time.
The shell embeds PostHog analytics with session recording disabled (disable_session_recording: true) and Do Not Track respected (respect_dnt: true).
Deployment is a Netlify CLI direct upload using a local personal access token that is gitignored and never committed.
netlify.toml disables post-processing (skip_processing = true) and registers a single SPA-style /* to /index.html redirect, so the artifact uploaded is exactly the artifact served.
A three-tier fallback chain (CLI direct upload preferred, Netlify MCP fallback, .site/deploy.sh last resort) keeps deploys reproducible; the preferred path does not consume Netlify build minutes.
Deploy is a first-class rotation phase with its own per-phase rubric, its own pending-issue lifecycle, and a cardinal rule that no vault failing Verify may be published.

Post-deploy verification runs four sub-checks against the production CDN: a manifest-count comparison, a deterministically sampled eight-page (five case briefs plus three topics) GET fetch, a search-sanity probe confirming search.json returns Marbury for the query judicial review, and a Source Materials HEAD sample; each failure mode opens a typed pending issue and blocks state advance.
The deployed site serves the professor's original source materials behind direct download links the build emits whenever a page wiki-links to a file under Source Materials/.
The _headers rules give source files long-lived caching (max-age=604800) while the generated JSON artifacts stay on short TTLs.

Every run begins with Step 0, which pulls submissions from the Netlify page-feedback form and triages each into the phase that can fix it (Lint for typos, Enrich for content gaps, Synthesize for new topics, Verify for disputed facts), fixing inline or logging a typed pending issue.

Each pending issue carries the page identifier, title, submitter identity, verbatim comment, and Netlify submission identifier; the scope-selection step of the next-running phase prefers pages with open professor-feedback issues routed to that phase.
The case study is a reviewed static site, not a chatbot; no LLM sits in the request path.
The published page is a stable HTML and JSON artifact, written and verified by the rotation phases at publish time and served by the CDN without further model inference.

Sajja, Sermet, Cwiertny and Demir (2023) present a platform-independent, curriculum-oriented intelligent assistant deployable as a conversational helper, cited as a representative chatbot-architecture contrast to the static-site case study.
Section XII develops the static-versus-chatbot contrast against contemporaneous chatbot architectures and the Magesh hallucination findings.
The workplan names a cost-and-labor table as one of the five most-important gaps the article must close before it can ship.
The existing record's single anchored figure is about sixty percent of weekly Claude usage consumed to reach the 198-page progress snapshot.
That anchored figure does not split by phase, by labor category, or by dollar count.
The workplan fixes the cost-table column set: hours by category (ingest, prompt tuning, review, debugging), token spend by phase, hosting cost, total dollars, and total person-hours.
The sixty-percent figure stays as the human-side starting anchor.

The per-phase and per-category breakdown lands through a retroactive reconstruction against the email trail, the git log, and best-memory entries committed to Appendix-Cost-Log.md, with prospective per-tick logging from the snapshot date forward.

The preferred deploy path is Netlify CLI direct upload from the scheduled task, which does not consume Netlify build minutes because the build runs in the local sandbox and only the produced assets cross the wire.
The Netlify MCP fallback is demoted because it does consume Netlify build minutes.
Under normal operation, the deploy phase lands at zero marginal hosting cost on the free tier.
When account credits exhaust, the free-tier ceiling reasserts itself as an HTTP 403 carrying the body 'Account credit usage exceeded'.

Three sequential credit-block events on May 7, 2026 at 18:41Z, 19:11Z, and 19:42Z tripped the dispatcher's three-strike guard, which skips the fast-deploy POST until human action restores credits or upgrades the tier.
The fast-deploy script completes in approximately six seconds and fits inside the forty-five-second sandbox cap.
The clean CLI-path deploy on the 205-page corpus logs approximately sixteen seconds build plus approximately eight seconds upload.
The Step 3.5 verification budget is approximately ten to fifteen seconds across the three sub-checks (page sample, search sanity probe, source-materials sample).
The full deploy-phase wall-clock floor reads as approximately twenty to forty seconds end-to-end depending on the upload path.
The vault scheduled task fires every thirty minutes with an Ingest budget of three to five files per run.
The article scheduled task fires every two hours, observable in the BUILD_NARRATIVE entry timestamps.

The vault Ingest cap is ten files per tick across new files and Step 8 backfills (fifteen when Steps 1 through 7 produce nothing), enforced by a scope_discipline score of zero (run score 4.5 instead of 5.0) when crossed.

Every scheduled-task run loads PROJECT_PRIMER, the state file, and the runbook section for the current phase as Tier 1, and the current phase's rubric, LESSONS, the current month's BUILD_NARRATIVE, and PERSONAS (Verify only) as Tier 2; other rubrics and archived narratives are not loaded.
The same tiered-context-loading architecture runs in the vault scheduled task per its own runbook and tiered-loading lesson.
The article's own L-007 names the cross-rubric-reading prohibition explicitly.
The four labor categories the workplan names map to the system's own phases (the body-prose mapping is the article's contribution, not the workplan's).

Ingest maps to the vault Ingest and Article Harvest phases; prompt tuning to per-tick rubric-and-LESSONS work plus Article Outline and Cite; review to per-tick scorecard reads, the LESSONS Consolidate sweep, and the Verify forced-finding pass; debugging to per-tick and multi-tick pending-issue resolution.
Three downstream consumers forward-reference this owning table: PI-003 for Section IV's ingest line, PI-018 for Section VIII's deploy line, and PI-042 for Section VII's iteration line.
PI-049 names the master cost-and-labor table reconstruction against the workplan's retroactive backfill protocol and frames it as still outstanding.
PI-050 names the external pricing lookups deferred to Cite for Anthropic API pricing, Netlify free-tier and upgrade pricing, and any metered MCP service prices.
PI-051 names the person-hours backfill across the four labor categories with honest confidence ranges, the methodology footnoted so a reader can replicate it against the same vault and git history.
